newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean minister quits amid bribery scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean minister quits amid bribery scandal.

text.p: South Korea's health minister stepped down on Wednesday amid bribery allegations involving his wife, becoming the second minister to leave under a corruption cloud in less than a month.
Lee Sung-ho, the Minister of Health and Welfare, submitted his resignation to President Kim Young-sam on Tuesday, shortly before state media reported Lee's wife was summoned by prosecutors.

The case has further embarrassed Kim, who has staked his reputation as an anti-corruption campaigner and whose drive to clean up South Korean society has brought to justice former presidents Roh Tae-woo and Chun Doo Hwan.
Last month Kim sacked his defence minister, Lee Yang-ho, who was formally charged on Monday with accepting bribes and leaking state secrets.
A Blue House statement said the health minister resigned "because his wife was suspected of taking bribes". Kim accepted the resignation on Wednesday.
"I feel bitter over this incident," Kim was quoted as saying. "In the future I will not condone anybody who is linked to corruption, regardless of whether their title is high or low."

State-run Korea Broadcasting System quoted unnamed prosecutors as saying Lee's wife, Park Sung-ae, was taken in for questioning on Tuesday night and had confessed to accepting 160 million won ($193,000) from an opticians' trade group.
The Korean Optometric Association had been seeking changes in the law giving its members a monopoloy over the sale of eyeglass frames, the television said.
It added that prosecutors planned to summon Lee as early as Wednesday.
Prosecution officials were not immediately available for comment, and an official at the optometric association declined to make any statement. There has been no word from Lee Sung-ho.
President Kim appointed a member of parliament for the ruling New Korea party, Sohn Hak-kyu, as his new health chief, the Blue House statement said.
"Kim Young-sam appointed Sohn Hak-kyu because he believes he is clean and able," the statement said.
"Since Kim's inauguration he has put emphasis on rooting out corruption and setting up morality and cleanliness among public officers," it added. Kim took office in 1993.
Former defence minister Lee was fired on October 17, hours before allegations that he received illicit pay-offs surfaced in the National Assembly.

Lee Yang-ho was charged with taking 150 million won as part of his share of payments to an American-Korean arms dealer from Daewoo Heavy Industries in connection with a military purchase of helicopters.
The former head of Daewoo Heavy, Sok Chin-chol, was also indicted along with two employees of the arms merchant.
Former president Roh is now appealing a 22-1/2 year jail sentence imposed for bribery, treason and mutiny. His predecessor, Chun, is trying to escape a death sentence on similar charges.
